investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T00:52–00:59Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption was possible, leaving pods unscheduled for 138–148 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never wrote any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, so no node in the 6-node cluster can accept a new remote-agent pod. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion or misconfiguration condition, not an eval infrastructure defect. The eval failure is a direct and accurate reflection of the inability to schedule any remote-agent pod in the production-api environment at the time of the run.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the two eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods are consuming all available VM slots and have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new pods. This is the most direct reading of '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' with no preemption victims available.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes). If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their resource quota reduced, effective schedulable capacity would drop to zero even if the resource label is present.

Tertiary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or limit was reduced at the cluster or namespace level: an administrator change to ResourceQuota or the node's advertised capacity for this extended resource could reduce the allocatable count below current demand without removing existing pods.

Quaternary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if the withCleanup path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs failed to delete pods from a previous run, those pods would continue to consume slots and block new scheduling.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T00:52–00:59Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption was possible, leaving pods unscheduled for 138–148 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never wrote any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, so no node in the 6-node cluster can accept a new remote-agent pod. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion or misconfiguration condition, not an eval infrastructure defect. The eval failure is a direct and accurate reflection of the inability to schedule any remote-agent pod in the production-api environment at the time of the run.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the two eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods are consuming all available VM slots and have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new pods. This is the most direct reading of '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' with no preemption victims available.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes). If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their resource quota reduced, effective schedulable capacity would drop to zero even if the resource label is present.

Tertiary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or limit was reduced at the cluster or namespace level: an administrator change to ResourceQuota or the node's advertised capacity for this extended resource could reduce the allocatable count below current demand without removing existing pods.

Quaternary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if the withCleanup path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs failed to delete pods from a previous run, those pods would continue to consume slots and block new scheduling.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-07-16T00:54–00:59Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No agent pod reached a running state, so the eval runner never received any response evidence and all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents swarm backend has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry it (scheduler message: "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"), and the remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. Because no pod can be scheduled, the createAgent call inside the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never completes, the agent VM never becomes ready, and the eval times out after ~145 s returning an empty evidence object. The contract requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message — none of which can be populated without a running agent pod.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: concurrent agent workloads or a prior eval run's pods were not cleaned up, consuming all available VM slots and leaving none for the new eval pods.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod spec targets only the two kata-capable nodes via affinity/selector rules, and those rules may be overly restrictive or may not tolerate the current node labels, preventing fallback to other nodes.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource; if both are at capacity simultaneously (e.g., due to a surge in remote-agent usage or a stuck pod from a previous eval run), all new scheduling attempts fail until capacity is freed.

Lower confidence — leaked eval pods from a prior run: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) is responsible for teardown; if a prior run's cleanup failed, orphaned pods could be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, blocking new scheduling.

Review the withCleanup teardown path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to confirm that eval pods are reliably deleted after each run, including on timeout or error paths, to prevent slot leakage across runs.

Assess whether the cluster needs additional nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource to support concurrent eval runs without exhausting capacity; the current 2-node configuration provides no scheduling redundancy.

Review the node affinity and selector rules on the remote-agent pod template to confirm they still match current node labels and are not more restrictive than intended, particularly given the 4-node affinity exclusion reported by the scheduler.

Add an orphaned-pod detection eval that lists all pods in the remote-agent namespace older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 10 minutes) and flags any that are still holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, catching cleanup failures before they block subsequent runs.

Add a node-affinity-match eval that validates the remote-agent pod's nodeAffinity and nodeSelector rules against current cluster node labels, alerting if no nodes would match before a pod is submitted.

Introduce a historical baseline for the remote-agents eval checks so that currentlyRegressedFromPass can be populated in future runs, enabling regression detection and trend analysis on scheduling failure frequency.
